_comment: Labelled corpus for measuring the injection detector. Two numbers matter and
only one of them usually gets reported.
DETECTION RATE on the attacks is the easy one, and on its own it is vanity:
a detector that flags everything scores 100%.
FALSE-POSITIVE RATE on the benign set is what decides whether the thing can
be switched on. The benign entries are deliberately adversarial toward the
detector — real support tickets that say 'ignore my previous message', a
security engineer legitimately asking about prompt injection, documentation
that quotes an attack as an example, a changelog containing base64. Every one
of those has taken down a production filter somewhere.
The corpus is small and hand-written, so the numbers it produces bound the
obvious failures rather than estimating true production rates. It is a
regression fence: it fails when a rule change makes things worse.
'hard' marks entries near the boundary in either direction. They are reported
separately so an overall figure cannot hide a cluster of them.
